title: Learner 01 | Day 160: Working increment: Capstone performance, cost, and incident recovery
body:
## Goal

Working increment: Capstone performance, cost, and incident recovery

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/adapters/versions.py`

**Method/unit:** `restore_model_version`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Heavy jobs are queued; per-workspace limits hold; model spend is bounded; an incident can be diagnosed and recovered locally.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **one observed gap in Capacity estimates and bottleneck analysis / Backups, restore, rollout, and rollback**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org one observed gap in Capacity estimates and bottleneck analysis Backups restore rollout`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** For this increment — Deliver a resumable, approved study-plan agent with a deterministic fallback and an operator-visible run history. — where are the input, state, failure, and output boundaries? Which trade-off did you choose?

**Review with @GlidingScorpion:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
